transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-12-01
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Lopez (Redwood CSM), Priya Raman (ClearPath PM), Jorge Alvarez (ClearPath Infra), Lena Park (ClearPath Security), Tom Brady (ClearPath ML)

Summary section (auto-gen, short): final go-live planning, focusing on cutover windows, canary approach, monitoring dashboards, and runbook owners. Action items captured.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh 3pm UTC, appreciate you carving the time out. main agenda — finalize cutover and canary plan. quick round robin?
[00:10] Priya: hi all, Priya here — we'll be the PM for the rollout. Jorge and Lena are on the infra/security side; Tom's from ML. We're targeting pilot -> prod next week if all checks pass.
[00:20] Alex: perfect. quick status: we've completed perf runs on dedicated nodes, ran a 10k sample workload, latency looks within SLO for 90th p95 p99, Samir will share details.
[00:33] Samir: yeah I ran the new quant profile, the 16-bit q4_0 path, um p95 120ms on our 8xA10 config for the 512 token window. there's some jitter at high concurrency but within the expected variance. spreadsheet link: https://redwood.io/drive/benchmarks (posted in chat).
[00:50] Tom: a couple clarifying q's — what's the expected token cost delta when we switch from hosted to dedicated? our finance folks want an estimate.
[00:58] Alex: good question. dedicated reduces per-token infra surcharge; overall token cost depends on batching and KV cache hit rate. Samir's spreadsheet includes a modelled token cost per 1M tokens for both hosted and dedicate variants.
[01:12] Samir: right now best estimate is ~20-30% lower unit cost on dedicated for our sample workload, depending on cache hit. i'll annotate assumptions in the sheet.
[01:25] Priya: ok timeline — we have a maintenance window Friday 02-Dec 02:00-06:00 UTC, is that enough for cutover?
[01:33] Alex: yes that's the window we had in mind. we recommend a staged canary: 5% traffic for 1 hour, then 20% for 2 hours, then 100% if no regressions. we can also do A/B style comparison for accuracy regressions — route 50/50 for a short period to compare outputs.
[01:50] Jorge: how will routing happen? do we need ip allowlist changes or new LB entries?
[01:55] Samir: routing is policy-driven in the control plane. for the private deployment you will have a VPC endpoint; we will need a short IP update for the canary hostnames, and we recommend pre-provisioning a canary shard pool. Jorge: okay so i'll prepare allowlist changes and pre-warm the canary nodes.
[02:15] Lena: security question — does switching to dedicated require new keys? how do you handle KMS/HSM; we have quarterly rotation windows to consider.
[02:22] Alex: Redwood supports customer-managed KMS. for the POC we used Redwood-managed keys; for pilot we recommend customer KMS so audit logs and rotation are aligned with your policy. we'll document the steps.
[02:35] Lena: pls note that our legal team needs 48 hours to review any key ceremony docs.
[02:40] Alex: noted. we'll get that to you by Thursday.
[02:44] Priya: runbooks — who owns the primary runbook and who is on-call post-cutover?
[02:49] Maya: from CSM side i'll coordinate the ops tabletop and keep the runbook template. Alex will draft the cutover_runbook_v1 and Samir will add technical steps and rollback commands. Priya to confirm who is on-call at ClearPath.
[03:02] Priya: i'll confirm the rotation, can assign Jorge and Tom as primary/secondary for the cutover window.
[03:08] Alex: rollback criteria — we propose automatic rollback if token latencies exceed 300ms at p95 or error rate >1% sustained for 5 minutes. also manual rollback triggers for accuracy regressions detected in A/B. thoughts?
[03:20] Tom: accuracy regressions — what tooling to compare outputs? we can send paired-requests to both endpoints and run an automated diff against our eval set.
[03:28] Samir: we support paired logging and can produce a side-by-side delta report, plus a basic perplexity/bleu style score for quick checks. we'll share a small script to run the comparator.
[03:40] Jorge: monitoring — what dashboards should we stand up? CPU/GPU utilization, queue depth, latency, error rate, token throughput, and cost burn. also audit logs for model calls.
[03:49] Samir: agreed. we'll push a Grafana dashboard template (redwood/prod-canary-dashboard) and CloudWatch/Prometheus exporter connectors depending on your infra.
[04:00] Priya: alerting thresholds?
[04:02] Samir: suggest p95 latency >200ms alert, error rate >0.5% warning, and >1% critical. also token burn > 150% expected forecast — cost alert. open to your thresholds.
[04:14] Lena: add security alerts for anomaly in request volume per client ID and any unknown IPs. we also need audit log retention details for compliance — how long do Redwood logs persist?
[04:23] Alex: current default is 90 days; for enterprise we can extend retention and ship to your SIEM. will include options in security pack doc.
[04:33] Priya: tabletop exercise, please explain format.
[04:36] Maya: 60-min session where we walk through runbook steps, simulate a latency spike and a required rollback, verify alerting and on-call responses. aim to validate people + process. proposed week of 2026-12-07.
[04:49] Priya: that works. ok next — legal/procurement check: any remaining agreements needed before pilot conversion?
[04:56] Alex: we need a signature on the pilot amendment for dedicated capacity and the data processing addendum. Maya will share the docs.
[05:02] Maya: i'll drop the pilot addendum and the security questionnaire to the legal thread today.
[05:06] Jorge: can we do a short perf spike test during the canary 20% phase? would like to validate tail latency under load.
[05:12] Samir: yes we can schedule a burn-in test for 20% window — controlled load generator with token-size distribution matching your prod. we'll coordinate timing.
[05:20] Tom: small nit — some of the earlier transcripts in our internal notes referred to "Red wood" which confused a few folks. pls use Redwood Inference consistently in docs.
[05:28] Alex: noted, thanks.
[05:30] Priya: anything else?
[05:32] Alex: quick recap: Alex send runbook draft + link by 12/03, Samir share perf spreadsheet by 12/02, Maya schedule tabletop week of 12/07, Priya confirm on-call by 12/04, Lena review KMS docs by 12/05, Jorge prepare allowlist and canary infra by 12/04. we'll aim for cutover in the Friday 02-Dec window pending legal signoff.
[05:55] Priya: thanks all. look forward to the runbook.
[05:58] Maya: i'll put calendar invites for the tabletop + follow-up.
[06:02] Alex: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email.

Notes on transcript quality: auto-transcript had some mislabels and occasional filler words, speaker overlap near the end. Some technical acronyms were expanded incorrectly (e.g., K-V cache, Redwood Dedicate).

References shared in chat: Cutover_Runbook_v1.md (draft), perf-benchmarks.xlsx (link: https://redwood.io/drive/benchmarks), security-pack.pdf (link to docs portal).
